# hostctl

[![Your dev tool to manage /etc/hosts like a pro!](docs/hostctl.png)](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/)

This tool gives you more control over the use of your hosts file. 
You can have multiple profiles and switch them on/off as you need.

## Why?

It is a tedious task to handle the `hosts` file by editing manually.
With this tool you can automate some aspects to do it cleaner and quick. 

## Features

  * Manage groups of host names by profile.
  * Enable/disable complete profiles.
  * Add/remove groups of host names.
  * Add profiles directly from a text file that you can add to your git repo or any VCS.
  * Sync a profile with Docker or Docker Compose containers.

## Documentation

You can read about how to use this tool here:

* [Getting started guide](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/getting-started/) 
* [Usage Guides](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/guides/)
* [CLI commands, options and flags](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/cli-usage/)

Or you can start directly on the [Docs homepage](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/).

## Sample Usage

![sample usage](docs/hostctl.gif)

## Installation

Go to [release page](https://github.com/guumaster/hostctl/releases) and download the binary you prefer.

Or read about other installation methods on different systems [here](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/installation/)

## Linux/Mac/Windows and permissions

The tool recognize your system and use the right hosts file, it will use `/etc/hosts` on Linux/Mac and `C:/Windows/System32/Drivers/etc/hosts` on Windows.

**SUDO/ADMIN**: You will need permissions for any action that modify hosts file, add `sudo` to the commands below when needed. If you are on windows, make sure you run it as administrator.

**WARNING**: it should work on any system. It's tested on Ubuntu and Windows 10. If you can confirm it works on other system, please let me know [here](https://github.com/guumaster/hostctl/issues/new).

## LICENSE

import subprocess, os, json
tmp="/tmp/testhosts"
def setc(cs): json.dump(cs,open("/tmp/mock_containers.json","w")); json.dump([],open("/tmp/mock_networks.json","w"))
def cont(id,names,networks): return {"Id":id,"Names":names,"NetworkSettings":{"Networks":networks}}
def net(ip): return {"NetworkID":"n","IPAddress":ip}

run("name no slash", cont("1",["web"],{"bridge":net("10.0.0.2")}))
run("empty names", cont("1",[],{"bridge":net("10.0.0.2")}))
run("two names", cont("1",["/a","/b"],{"bridge":net("10.0.0.2")}))
run("empty ip", cont("1",["/noip"],{"bridge":net("")}))
run("no networks", cont("1",["/nonet"],{}))
run("bad ip", cont("1",["/bad"],{"bridge":net("notip")}))

run("network nil ip field missing", cont("1",["/x"],{"bridge":{}}))

hostctl is a CLI tool to manage your hosts file with ease.
You can have multiple profiles, enable/disable exactly what
you need each time with a simple interface.

Usage:
  hostctl [command]

Available Commands:
  add         Add content to a profile in your hosts file.
  backup      Creates a backup copy of your hosts file
  disable     Disable a profile from your hosts file.
  enable      Enable a profile on your hosts file.
  help        Help about any command
  list        Shows a detailed list of profiles on your hosts file.
  remove      Remove a profile from your hosts file.
  replace     Replace content to a profile in your hosts file.
  restore     Restore hosts file content from a backup file.
  status      Shows a list of profile names and statuses on your hosts file.
  sync        Sync some system IPs with a profile.
  toggle      Change status of a profile on your hosts file.

Flags:
  -c, --column strings     Column names to show on lists. comma separated
  -h, --help               help for hostctl
      --host-file string   Hosts file path (default "/etc/hosts")
      --no-color           force colorless output
  -o, --out string         Output type (table|raw|markdown|json) (default "table")
  -q, --quiet              Run command without output
      --raw                Output without borders (same as -o raw)
  -v, --version            version for hostctl

Use "hostctl [command] --help" for more information about a command.

import subprocess, os, sys, shutil, difflib, json

REF="/workspace/executable"

WORK="/tmp/cmpwork"
INPUT="/tmp/cmp_input.txt"

def prepare(case):
    shutil.rmtree(WORK, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(WORK)
    # aux files
    for path,content in case.get("aux",{}).items():
        p=path.replace("{WORK}",WORK).replace("{INPUT}",INPUT)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True) if os.path.dirname(p) else None
        mode="wb" if isinstance(content,bytes) else "w"
        with open(p,mode) as f: f.write(content)
    initial=case.get("initial")
    if initial is None:
        try: os.remove(HOST)
        except: pass
    else:
        mode="wb" if isinstance(initial,bytes) else "w"
        with open(HOST,mode) as f: f.write(initial)

def run_scenario(exe, case):
    prepare(case)
    out=[]
    for i,step in enumerate(case["steps"]):
        args=[a.replace("{HOST}",HOST).replace("{WORK}",WORK).replace("{INPUT}",INPUT) for a in step.get("args",[])]
        stdin_spec=step.get("stdin",("pipe",b""))
        kwargs={}
        if stdin_spec[0]=="pipe": kwargs["input"]=stdin_spec[1]
        elif stdin_spec[0]=="devnull": kwargs["stdin"]=subprocess.DEVNULL
        elif stdin_spec[0]=="file": kwargs["stdin"]=open(stdin_spec[1].replace("{WORK}",WORK),"rb")
        env={"PATH":os.environ["PATH"],"TERM":"dumb"}
        env.update(step.get("env",{}))
        if case.get("env"): env.update(case["env"])
        try:
            r=subprocess.run([exe]+args, capture_output=True, cwd=step.get("cwd",WORK).replace("{WORK}",WORK) if isinstance(step.get("cwd",WORK),str) else WORK, env=env, timeout=step.get("timeout",5), **kwargs)
            out.append(f"STEP {i} args={args} exit={r.returncode}\nSTDOUT={r.stdout!r}\nSTDERR={r.stderr!r}")
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
            out.append(f"STEP {i} args={args} TIMEOUT stdout={e.stdout!r} stderr={e.stderr!r}")
        if os.path.exists(HOST):
            try: content=open(HOST,"rb").read()
            except Exception as e: content=f"<err {e}>".encode()
            out.append(f"HOSTFILE={content!r}")
        else:
            out.append("HOSTFILE=<missing>")
        for path in step.get("capture",[]):
            p=path.replace("{WORK}",WORK).replace("{INPUT}",INPUT).replace("{HOST}",HOST)
            if os.path.isdir(p):
                listing=sorted(os.listdir(p)); out.append(f"DIR {path}={listing}")
                for name in listing:
                    fp=os.path.join(p,name)
                    if os.path.isfile(fp): out.append(f"  FILE {name}={open(fp,'rb').read()!r} mode={oct(os.stat(fp).st_mode & 0o777)}")
            elif os.path.exists(p):
                out.append(f"FILE {path}={open(p,'rb').read()!r} mode={oct(os.stat(p).st_mode & 0o777)}")
            else:
                out.append(f"FILE {path}=<missing>")
        # also capture workdir listing if requested at case level
        if case.get("capture_work"):
            listing=sorted(os.listdir(WORK)); out.append(f"WORKDIR={listing}")
            for name in listing:
                fp=os.path.join(WORK,name)
                if os.path.isfile(fp): out.append(f"  WFILE {name}={open(fp,'rb').read()!r}")
    return "\n".join(out)+"\n"
